1. (Currently amended) A method of analyzing one or more plant embryos comprising: (a) collecting shed cellular material from one or more embryos by agitating the one or more embryos in a non-destructive medium; (b) obtaining DNA from the shed cellular material; (c) performing a molecular analysis of the DNA obtained in step (b); and (d) germinating at least one of said one or more embryos, wherein the collected cellular material is not subjected to chemical disruption that adversely affects embryo viability.  
2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the non-destructive medium consists essentially of water or a composition that maintains embryo viability.  
7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein DNA is obtained by incubating the shed cellular material with a cell wall degrading enzyme that does not adversely affect embryo viability.  
11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the one or more embryos are immature embryos harvested in a manner that maintains viability.  
12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 further comprising storing the one or more embryos in a manner that preserves viability, prior to step (c) or (d).  
13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said molecular analysis is genotyping performed on DNA that has been minimally processed to maintain fidelity.  
17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 further comprising selecting one or more embryos based on genotype analysis of DNA obtained from said embryos, wherein the selection criteria do not adversely impact embryo viability.  
18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 17 further comprising germinating the one or more selected embryos, wherein the germination process ensures that the embryos remain viable throughout the process.  
19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 18 wherein any of the steps resulting in selection of one or more embryos is automated and does not adversely affect the viability of said embryos.
